goals.d: Reach $1.8M in booked revenue for 2026 without compromising the craftsmanship standard that commands premium pricing.
Hold the pipeline at 3–4× the next quarter's revenue target so signed work stays lined up with crew availability.
Keep gross margin above 33% and a 90+ quality score on every completed job through crew training and scoring.

highlight: Pipeline reached $780K in July, up 8.3% from June and $260K since February, the clearest signal that the year is on track. Booked revenue stands at $1.44M, roughly 80% of the $1.8M goal and ahead of the seasonal pace with more work still to build. Backlog sits at 5.1 months of scheduled work, so crews are booked out well into Q4. A deep, high-intent pipeline and a full backlog are the clearest signs that the months ahead are well covered.

takeaways.d: Pipeline hit $780K, up 8% for the month. A deep, high-intent pipeline is the best early read on whether 2026 lands on plan, and whether crews stay booked.
Booked revenue reached $1.44M, 80% of goal by July, carried by the spring/summer build season and a signed six-figure fall addition.
5.1 months of booked work means crews are scheduled deep into Q4. The constraint has quietly shifted from finding work to building it without thinning the crew's standard.

insights.t: Capacity Is the Ceiling, Not Leads
insights.d: With 5 months of backlog, demand isn't the limit. Skilled crew is. The growth lever is training people to hold the standard so the next big job doesn't dilute quality.
A 95 quality score is why you win premium bids. Score every completed job so the standard is measured, not assumed, and so new hires can be trained and held to it.
Tickets swing from $15K patios to $250K additions, so margin has to be defended per job. Estimate-vs-actual on labor and material keeps big jobs from quietly eroding profit.

actions.t: Score Every Completed Job on Craftsmanship
bullets: Define a simple 5-point scorecard: joint work, alignment, cleanliness, material match, client sign-off.
Score each finished job and review it with the crew so the standard stays visible.
actions.step: Build a one-page quality scorecard and score your last 3 completed jobs this week to set the baseline.

bullets: List every open opportunity with its dollar value and win probability; total the weighted pipeline.
Keep coverage at 3–4× next quarter and flag the big jobs that carry the year.
actions.step: Put all open estimates into one sheet with value × probability and total your weighted pipeline this week.

bullets: Compare bid vs. actual labor and material on recent jobs; feed the gaps into the next bid.
Tie a quality bonus to crews that hit both their score and their margin.
actions.step: Pull your last 3 jobs and calculate true labor + material cost against the estimate.

actions.t: Put Your Financial Strength to Work
bullets: Set a dedicated CAPEX / expansion fund for a major investment: equipment, a second crew, or a facility.
Or begin structured exit and succession planning to protect the value you've built.
actions.step: Meet with your accountant this month to set a reserve target and decide: reinvest for growth, or begin an exit / succession plan.

challenge: The focus is keeping a high-quality, high-intent pipeline lined up so signed work flows smoothly into crew availability, no idle weeks, no rushed scheduling. That means qualifying leads for fit and readiness, sequencing projects to the crew calendar, and protecting the craftsmanship standard as the schedule fills. Get that rhythm right and the business runs at full capacity without ever trading away quality for speed.
closing: You've built a business people pay a premium for. Keep the pipeline full, hold the line on margin, and score every job so the standard is measured, not assumed. Do that, and you can take on more of the big work without ever thinning the quality that got you here.
